title: Gnanasara Thera calls for international probe into Easter Sunday attacks
byline: Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, General Secretary of the Bodu Bala Sena (BBS), has called on all responsible parties, including Malcolm Cardinal Ranjith, to cease what he described as “acting” in efforts to identify those involved in the Easter Sunday attacks and instead hand over the investigations to an independent international inquiry.

title: Malinga, Madushanka rip through DC as SRH surge to third after Abhishek blitz
byline: Sunrisers Hyderabad rode a fiery spell from their Sri Lankan quicks to seal a commanding 47-run win over Delhi Capitals, climbing to third on the IPL 2026 points table after a headline-grabbing century from Abhishek Sharma.

title: US announces ceasefire extension with Iran
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would indefinitely ​extend the ceasefire with Iran, hours before it was set to expire, to allow the two countries to continue peace talks ‌to end a war that has killed thousands of people and shaken the global economy.

title: 161 school-age children not attending school in Kalutara
byline: A total of 161 children of school-going age who are not attending school have been identified in the Kalutara District in 2025, with the highest number reported from the Dodangoda Divisional Secretariat Division.

title: Gold rises as oil weakens after US extends ceasefire with Iran
byline: Gold prices firmed on Wednesday as lower oil prices, following a U.S. extension of a ceasefire with Iran, eased ‌fears of an inflation spike and prolonged high interest rates.

title: Over 10,000 pets suffer in fireworks fallout
byline: The festive cheer of the Sinhala and Tamil New Year has come under sharp criticism, with veterinary experts claiming that more than 10,000 cats and dogs have suffered hearing damage and disorientation due to firecrackers and fireworks.

title: Easter probe under threat; families allege sabotage
byline: Family members of the Easter Sunday attacks say they are cautiously optimistic about the ongoing investigations, but have raised serious concerns over what they describe as attempts by various parties to sabotage the process.

title: Sri Lanka on the brink of a crippling medicine shortage
byline: Sri Lanka is on the brink of a crippling medicine shortage, including essential and life saving medicines, that threatens to paralyze both public and private healthcare sectors, the Sri Lanka Chamber of the Pharmaceutical Industry (SLCPI) warned yesterday.

title: Political parties to tone down May Day this year
byline: Political parties are to tone down May Day celebrations as it falls on a full moon day this year. The ruling party has also decided to celebrate May Day at district level.

title: Officials of ‘Deep State’ obstructing investigations on Easter Sunday attacks: Cardinal
byline: Highlighting that there is a ‘Deep State’ that controls the present government, Archbishop of Colombo Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith yesterday alleged that those officers in the deep state are out to obstruct the investigations on Easter Sunday attacks.

title: Shammi Silva bowled out
byline: Anti-corruption crusaders and die-hard cricket followers in the island could breathe a sigh of relief as President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has at last bowed down to ground realities and ordered Sri Lanka Cricket’s (SLC) merry-go-round dictator Shammi Silva to clear out.

title: Sri Lanka tightens terror financing controls with TFS
byline: The Ministry of Defence said Sri Lanka has strengthened its national security framework by placing renewed emphasis on Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS), a key tool used to disrupt the financing of terrorism and safeguard the country’s financial system.

title: Dollar at week high as markets raise doubts over Iran ceasefire
byline: The dollar steadied in early Asian trade on Wednesday, as skepticism over U.S. ​President Donald Trump’s announcement of an indefinite extension of a ceasefire with Iran lifted demand for the safe-haven ‌currency, pushing it to a one-week high.

title: US announces ceasefire extension with Iran
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would indefinitely ​extend the ceasefire with Iran, hours before it was set to expire, to allow the two countries to continue peace talks ‌to end a war that has killed thousands of people and shaken the global economy.

title: SL recovery on edge as Middle East shock ripples through economy: CBSL
byline: Sri Lanka’s economic recovery is entering a more fragile phase, with the Central Bank warning that rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are beginning to test the resilience built through recent stabilisation efforts, even as domestic conditions remain broadly supportive of growth.

title: Thundershowers with lightning expected after 1 p.m.
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a weather advisory warning of thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning in several parts of the country later today.

title: Airbus probe: Warrant issued on Kapila Chandrasena’s wife
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Isuru Neththikumara today issued a warrant on Priyanka Nayomali Wijenayake, the wife of former SriLankan Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena, over the investigations into the Airbus transaction.

title: Middle East volatility threatens Sri Lanka’s food security: WFP
byline: Rising instability in the Middle East is posing growing risks to Sri Lanka’s household food security, the World Food Programme (WFP) has warned in a recent report.

title: Former Health Ministry chief legal officer remanded over bribery allegations
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested a retired Chief Legal Officer of the Ministry of Health on charges of soliciting and accepting a significant bribe related to a government building lease.

title: Rupee continues to weaken against US Dollar
byline: The Sri Lankan rupee further depreciated against the US dollar across commercial banks on Wednesday (22), with selling rates hovering around the Rs. 320 mark.

title: Japan pledges USD 2.66 million for climate resilience and gender equality projects in Sri Lanka
byline: The Government of Japan has announced USD 2.66 million in funding for two new development projects in Sri Lanka aimed at strengthening climate resilience and promoting gender equality in vulnerable communities.

title: SJB extends open invitation to UNP for its May Day rally
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) today extended an open invitation to the United National Party (UNP) to join its May Day rally to be held at the P.D. Sirisena Grounds on May 1.

title: World’s biggest maker of condoms set to raise prices due to Iran war
byline: The boss of the world’s biggest condom maker, Karex, says the firm will raise its prices by up to 30% or possibly more if the Iran war continues to disrupt supplies of the raw materials used in its products.

title: US may run out of missiles if another war breaks out: Report
byline: The US military has “significantly depleted” its stockpile of key missiles during the war in Iran and could face shortages in a future conflict, CNN reported Tuesday.

title: Three vessels hit, two seized by IRGC, Iranian media say
byline: Iranian media are reporting that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted the three ships hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Govt approves committee to monitor Easter probe progress
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the establishment of a new mechanism to monitor the implementation of recommendations related to the Easter Sunday attacks.

title: China completes 2026 school uniform donation for over 4.4 million students
byline: Certificates were officially exchanged today (22) confirming the completion of the full provision of school uniforms for 2026, donated by the Republic of China.

title: Court orders continued detention of former SIS Director Suresh Sallay
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Isuru Neththikumara today ordered that the detention order issued against former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Rtd.) Suresh Sallay, will remain in effect.

title: Cabinet clears Rs. 356M consultancy for railway expansion to Ratnapura
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the awarding of a consultancy contract for the feasibility study and preparation of detailed plans to extend the Kelani Valley Railway Line from Avissawella to Ratnapura.

title: Iraj Chaminda Pathiraja appointed acting Immigration Controller General
byline: Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on May 19, 2025 to appoint Mr. Iraj Chaminda Pathiraja, an officer in the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, on a full-time acting basis as the Controller General of Immigration and Emigration.

title: Government approves procurement of 800,000 dialysis solution bags for kidney patients
byline: The government  has approved the procurement of 800,000 bags of peritoneal dialysis solutions used in the treatment of patients suffering from chronic kidney failure, on the recommendation of the Health and Mass Media Minister.

title: Former MP Premalal Jayasekara granted bail
byline: Former Ratnapura District Parliamentarian Premalal Jayasekara, who was arrested by the Nuwara Eliya Police on Monday (21) over allegations of threatening a person with a firearm during an incident in the Nuwara Eliya area, was produced before the Nuwara Eliya Magistrate’s Court today (22).

title: Cabinet approves SriLankan Airlines handling contracts in Dubai
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the awarding of contracts for ground and cargo handling services for SriLankan Airlines at Dubai International Airport (DXB).

title: Cabinet approves new methodology for issuing inter-provincial passenger transport permits
byline: The Cabinet Ministers has approved a new methodology for the issuance of inter-provincial passenger transport permits, aimed at restructuring and streamlining the country’s public transport permit system.

title: Two cargo ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz after Trump extends ceasefire
byline: Two cargo ships have reportedly come under fire in the Strait of Hormuz, the British maritime agency has said.

title: South Korean fighter jets collided due to pilots snapping pictures, report finds
byline: South Korean authorities have found that two fighter jets collided mid-air in 2021 because the pilots were taking pictures and videos.

title: Taiwan president cancels trip after African countries revoke flight permits
byline: Taiwan President Lai Ching-te has cancelled a presidential trip to the southern African nation of Eswatini, accusing Beijing of putting pressure on other countries to bar his aircraft from flying over their territories.

title: UK moves to ban smoking for everyone born after 2008
byline: Children who do not reach the age of 18 before January 1, 2027 will never be permitted to buy cigarettes or tobacco products in the UK, once a new law that has now completely cleared parliament gets royal assent from King Charles III.

title: Sri Lanka embassy in Riyadh introduces special consular services
byline: The Embassy of Sri Lanka in Riyadh has announced the introduction of a Special Weekend Consular Services Programme to assist Sri Lankan expatriates in Saudi Arabia who are unable to access services during regular working days.

title: Namal questions treasury controls after US$2.5 million fraud loss
byline: The reported loss of US$2.5 million through fraudulent payment instructions is not a minor financial lapse but a serious breakdown in oversight, internal controls and institutional safeguards within the Treasury, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa has said.

title: LPL 2026 to be held from July 10 to August 5
byline: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026 is scheduled to be held from July 10 to August 5, marking the sixth edition of Sri Lanka’s premier domestic T20 competition.

title: Measles cases reappear despite strong immunisation record
byline: Health authorities have warned of a resurgence in measles cases in Sri Lanka, despite the country’s long-standing and successful immunisation programme spanning more than six decades.

title: Thirteen killed in second India fireworks blast in three days
byline: At least 13 people have been killed in an explosion at a firecracker factory in India’s southern state of Kerala, officials say.

title: CID produces former SIS chief Suresh Sallay before court
byline: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) produced former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Rtd.) Suresh Sallay, before the Fort Magistrate’s court today in connection with investigations into the Easter Sunday bomb attacks.

title: Tornado damages school, dozens of houses in Wariyapola
byline: A tornado that struck Wariyapola last night caused extensive damage to property, including a two-story building at Sri Gnanodaya National School, officials said.

title: EU mandates replaceable phone batteries by 2027: Major shift for iPhone and Android users
byline: The European Union is set to introduce a major shift in smartphone design. As of February 18, 2027, user-replaceable batteries should be included in all smartphones and tablets sold within the bloc. The relocation is part of a bigger initiative to lessen electronic waste and prolong the lifetime of consumer devices.

title: Premalal Jayasekara produced before Nuwara Eliya Court over firearm incident
byline: Former Ratnapura District MP Premalal Jayasekara was produced before the Nuwara Eliya Magistrate’s Court today (22) following his arrest over an alleged firearm-related incident.

title: Two Pakistani astronauts selected as candidates for China space programme
byline: China has ​selected two Pakistani ‌astronauts as candidates for ​its manned ​space programme, state broadcaster ⁠CCTV ​reported on Wednesday.

title: Tamil Nadu elections: Banners supporting Vijay, Seeman, Stalin displayed in Jaffna
byline: Banners supporting Tamil Nadu political leaders have been displayed across several areas in Jaffna in connection with the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly elections.

title: Complaint already lodged with law enforcement agencies over theft by cyber hackers: Ministry
byline: The Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development said it has already lodged complaints with law enforcement agencies and other relevant institutions regarding the theft committed by cyber hackers who breached the computer system of the External Resources Department of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development.

title: Five-member team probes missing $2.5m Australian loan installment
byline: The Finance, Planning and Economic Development Ministry has appointed a five-member technical committee to investigate the disappearance of more than USD 2.5 million (approximately Rs. 8 million) paid as an installment of an Australian loan.

title: Finance Ministry will clarify on missing USD 2.5 million: Nalinda
byline: While admitting reports of US dollars 2.5 million paid by the Treasury as a debt payment reportedly falling into the hands of a cyber hacker, the government said the Speaker will decide whether to appoint a committee to probe the incident after studying the letter sent by PC Maithri Gunaratne on the matter.

title: Harsha questions why Finance Ministry, Central Bank silent on missing USD 2.5 million
byline: Claiming that Parliament is Constitutionally responsible for public finance, Chairman of the Committee on Public Finance (CoPF) and SJB MP Dr. Harsha De Silva raised concerns why the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) have been silent all this time regarding the loss of USD 2.5 million of the Sri Lankan peoples’ money.

title: AG can indict State officials who fail to assist Easter attack probe: Court
byline: While emphasizing over the investigations conducted into the Easter Sunday bomb attacks, Colombo Fort Magistrate Isuru Neththikumara said that all State officials, including the Army Commander and the Director of Army Intelligence, must extend their support to the Attorney General in the investigations being carried out in relation to retired Major General Suresh Sallay,
